title: The Insurance CEO’s Blueprint for Scaling AI
gist: BCG argues insurers must replace scattered AI pilots with CEO-led, enterprise-wide shared capabilities across six priorities, from AI discoverability and a common conversational layer to agentic software delivery. It cites 50-70% call containment, 30-60% underwriting/claims efficiency gains, 3-5x productivity for fully agentic development, and says 30-40% of existing project budgets can be redirected, with 70% of effort going to people and processes.

themes.theme: Pilot sprawl vs enterprise AI capabilities

insights.claim: Many insurers run dozens of AI pilots inside individual businesses or functions but lack an enterprise approach that converts them into scalable capabilities, held back by uncertainty over proven value, the pace of technology change, and short-term performance pressure favoring narrow low-risk use cases.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Insurers reporting many AI pilots but no shared platform are likely under-delivering on AI value; pilot counts are not a proxy for progress.
insights.quote: They run dozens of pilots, often within individual businesses or functions, but lack an enterprise approach that turns those efforts into scalable capabilities.
insights.locator: AI is reshaping the retail insurance

insights.claim: Insurers should organize AI around a common set of horizontal capabilities shared across P&C, health, distribution and other units, with business units retaining responsibility for application while no longer building the same underlying solutions independently.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Favors insurers with centralized AI platforms and strong CEO authority over federated, siloed carriers.
insights.quote: Business units retain responsibility for how those capabilities are applied and adapted, but they no longer need to develop the same underlying solutions independently.

insights.claim: Scaling AI in insurance requires the CEO to personally make cross-boundary decisions on where to concentrate investment, what to build once, what tools businesses control, and which legacy initiatives to resize or stop.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: AI transformation is a governance problem; watch for CEO-level ownership as a leading indicator of execution.
insights.quote: insurance CEOs need to take the lead in making those decisions

insights.claim: BCG frames six CEO priority areas for insurance AI: AI visibility and access, an enterprise conversational layer, AI-enabled process redesign, AI-assisted service, AI-supported sales, and AI-enabled technology delivery.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Provides a checklist to benchmark insurer AI strategies across the front door, operations and IT.

themes.theme: AI as the new insurance front door

insights.claim: Third-party AI tools are becoming a gateway to the retail insurance market, and insurers that are hard for AI to find or engage with risk being excluded from consideration before a customer ever reaches them.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Distribution power may shift to AI intermediaries, threatening direct-brand advantages of carriers that neglect AI discoverability.
insights.quote: insurers that are difficult for it to find or engage with risk being excluded from the buying journey before a customer ever reaches them

insights.claim: Insurers' response to AI-mediated buying unfolds in three stages: discoverable (AI can find current product information), conversational (AI-enabled experiences to continue with the insurer), and transactional (AI agents query systems, generate quotes and eventually bind coverage).
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Carriers with APIs that let agents quote and bind will be positioned for agent-driven distribution.
insights.locator: The response unfolds in three stages.

insights.claim: Agent-to-agent insurance transactions are likely to emerge first in B2B markets before potentially extending to consumer insurance.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Commercial lines and brokers are the early testbed for agentic distribution; consumer impact lags.
insights.quote: This agent-to-agent interaction is likely to emerge first in B2B markets but could ultimately extend to consumer insurance as well.
insights.locator: The response unfolds in three stages.

insights.claim: Letting each line of business build its own AI customer-service capability risks re-creating the fragmentation AI should eliminate; a common conversational layer across businesses and channels should handle routine requests and hand complex cases to humans.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Duplicated line-level chatbots are a red flag for wasted spend and new silos.
insights.quote: insurers that apply AI in customer service can potentially re-create the fragmentation that AI should help eliminate

insights.claim: In BCG's experience an enterprise conversational layer can achieve call containment of 50% to 70% and service-to-sales improvements of 20% to 30%, depending on starting point, volumes and processes.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Implies large contact-center cost reduction plus revenue uplift for insurers that deploy shared conversational AI.
insights.quote: call containment of 50% to 70% and service-to-sales improvements of 20% to 30% are achievable
insights.locator: The potential value is already substantial.

insights.claim: A shared conversational layer is especially valuable in structurally high-churn businesses such as P&C and supplementary health, where cross-relationship interaction data can improve retention while lowering servicing costs.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Retention gains in high-churn lines compound into lifetime value, not just cost savings.
insights.quote: particularly valuable in businesses with structurally higher churn, such as P&C and supplementary health
insights.locator: A shared capability also creates benefits

themes.theme: Process redesign in underwriting and claims

insights.claim: Underwriting and claims require risk judgment, coverage interpretation and specialized expertise, so they warrant tailored AI solutions and dedicated teams; AI-enabled redesign can generate 30% to 60% efficiency gains there, with more in selected processes.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Core insurance operations, not just front-office chat, hold the largest efficiency pool.
insights.quote: AI-enabled redesign can generate efficiency gains of 30% to 60% in these areas, with even greater gains possible in selected processes

insights.claim: AI-enabled redesign of underwriting and claims can contribute to a better combined ratio through better underwriting decisions, lower claims costs, more new business and higher customer satisfaction.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Links AI directly to the key P&C profitability metric; watch combined ratio trends of AI leaders.
insights.quote: contribute to a better combined ratio

insights.claim: Insurers should redesign core processes end to end rather than automate piecemeal, and centralize infrastructure and reusable components for standard administrative work like data extraction instead of addressing it function by function.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Back-office automation should be bought or built once as shared infrastructure.
insights.locator: The surrounding administrative and processing work

insights.claim: Agent-assist tools that listen in real time, retrieve information and suggest next steps have produced early efficiency gains of 20% to 50% and reductions in call transfers of as much as 90%.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Human-in-the-loop AI delivers sizable gains even where full automation is inappropriate.
insights.quote: early implementations have produced efficiency gains of 20% to 50% and reductions in call transfers of as much as 90%

insights.claim: Insurers should reinvest some AI-released service capacity into higher-quality human interactions for complex cases like disputed claims or serious health conditions, rather than pursuing efficiency alone.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Pure cost-cutting narratives may miss churn-reduction upside from better human service.
insights.quote: But the goal should not be efficiency alone.

insights.claim: As AI absorbs transactional work, human advice may become more important for complex or financially consequential insurance purchases, so AI should free sales agents to sell rather than replace them.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Argues against the thesis that AI disintermediates insurance agents for complex products.
insights.quote: human advice may become more important for complex or financially consequential insurance-buying decisions

insights.claim: AI digital twins for sales agents that prepare quotes, handle paperwork and cultivate leads can cut agents' administrative burden by 40% to 50%, and can reuse technology already built for customer-facing AI.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Reuse of customer-facing AI creates a second return on the same investment.
insights.quote: these capabilities can reduce the administrative burden on sales agents by 40% to 50%

insights.claim: BCG defines three maturity levels for AI in insurer technology delivery: AI-assisted (10% to 20% productivity gain), AI-driven with generative output under oversight (25% to 40%), and fully agentic across the software lifecycle (3x to 5x productivity).
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Fully agentic development implies step-change IT productivity that could accelerate legacy modernization.
insights.locator: The opportunity can be viewed across three levels

insights.claim: CEOs should have the technology function set a quantified ambition and target maturity level per team rather than pursuing maximum automation everywhere.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Differentiated, measured automation targets signal mature AI governance.
insights.quote: rather than pursuing maximum automation everywhere

themes.theme: Funding and people levers for scale

insights.claim: In BCG's experience 30% to 40% of resources planned in existing insurer project portfolios can be repurposed toward high-value AI priorities by resizing or stopping initiatives, funding subsequent investment waves.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: AI transformation can be largely self-funded, limiting incremental budget needs.
insights.quote: 30% to 40% of resources planned in existing project portfolios can potentially be repurposed

insights.claim: BCG holds that roughly 10% of AI transformation effort should go to algorithms, 20% to technology and data, and 70% to people and processes, because mindsets and skills are harder to upgrade than technology.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Execution capacity in change management, not model access, is the binding constraint on AI value.
insights.quote: roughly 10% of the effort in an AI transformation should go to algorithms, 20% to technology and data, and 70% to people and processes

insights.claim: Insurers should adopt an AI-first mindset assuming AI can perform the work unless there is a reason it cannot, while concentrating on a limited number of high-value priorities with accountable owners.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Concentrated bets with named owners outperform scattered portfolios.
insights.quote: starting from the assumption that AI can perform the work unless there is a reason it cannot

insights.claim: Insurers should select a limited set of complementary AI partners, avoiding both single-provider dependence and a proliferation of overlapping vendors that recreates silos at the enterprise level.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Vendor consolidation favors a few broad AI platform providers over niche point solutions in insurance.
insights.locator: Have we assembled the right ecosystem

insights.claim: The future differentiator among insurance CEOs will be not whether they embrace AI but how effectively they enable organizations to apply it faster, better and at greater scale through reusable shared capabilities.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Competitive advantage accrues to scaled executors, widening dispersion among carriers.
insights.quote: what will increasingly set insurance CEOs apart is not whether they embrace AI, but how effectively they enable their organizations to apply it
